title: Make the busy-workers gauge see virtual threads

blocks.text: The checkout service's dashboard has a "busy workers" gauge, and the autoscaler adds instances when it stays above 80% of capacity. The gauge used to count the live threads whose names started with `checkout-`. Since checkout moved to virtual threads, the gauge reads 0 at the busiest hour of the day, and the autoscaler has stopped adding instances.

`WorkerGauge` is the `ThreadFactory` the service now uses, with `Executors.newThreadPerTaskExecutor(gauge)`. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/WorkerGauge.java`: `newThread(...)` makes the thread for one request, and `busy()` reports how many of this gauge's requests are in progress. About eight lines in total.
When you're done, `busy()` follows the requests that are running: up while they run or wait, down when they end, however they end.

cases.says: each request runs on a virtual thread named with the gauge's prefix
busy() reports the requests in progress on virtual threads, and 0 once they are done
a request that throws is no longer counted once its thread ends
a thread that was made but not started is not counted

origin.section: Thread Listings Leave Virtual Threads Out

concepts: Thread.getAllStackTraces() and ThreadMXBean see only platform threads, so a gauge built on them reads 0 for virtual threads; count the work in the code that starts and ends it.
